condition: Acute gastroenteritis with dehydration and AKI
admission_note:
TIRUMALA MULTISPECIALITY HOSPITAL, HYDERABAD

PATIENT NAME: Mr. Prakash Sharma
AGE/SEX: 52/M
UHID: 240510-9832
ADMISSION DATE: 10/05/24

DIAGNOSIS:
1. Acute Gastroenteritis with Moderate Dehydration
2. Hyponatremia
3. Acute Kidney Injury (AKI) on evaluation

CHIEF COMPLAINTS:
1. Multiple loose stools x 2 days
2. Vomiting x 1 day
3. Decreased urine output x 1 day

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
Patient, a 52-year-old male, was in his usual state of health until 2 days ago when he developed loose, watery stools, about 15-20 episodes per day, non-mucoid, not associated with blood. This was followed by 5-6 episodes of non-bilious, non-bloody vomiting since yesterday, containing food particles. He complains of generalized weakness, dizziness on standing and significant reduction in urine volume for the past 24 hours. He tried over-the-counter medication (Lopiramide) with no relief. Due to persisting symptoms and increasing weakness, he has presented here for further management.

PAST HISTORY:
Known case of Hypertension for 5 years, on regular treatment with TAB TELMA-H (40mg/12.5mg) 1-0-0. 
No known history of Diabetes Mellitus, Tuberculosis, Asthma, or Thyroid disorder. No known drug allergies.

PERSONAL HISTORY:
Mixed diet. Non-smoker. Occasional alcohol consumption.

GENERAL EXAMINATION:
Patient is conscious, oriented, appears tired and dehydrated. 
VITALS: BP: 90/60 mmHg, PR: 110/min, feeble, RR: 18/min, SpO2: 97% at room air, Temp: 99.0°F.
Signs of dehydration present: dry tongue, decreased skin turgor, sunken eyes. No pallor, icterus, cyanosis, clubbing or pedal edema.

SYSTEMIC EXAMINATION:
CVS: S1, S2 heard. Tachycardia present. No murmurs.
RS: Air entry bilaterally equal, no added sounds.
P/A: Soft, non-tender. Bowel sounds are hyperactive.
CNS: GCS 15/15. No focal neurological deficits.

INVESTIGATIONS:
Blood sent for CBC, RFT, S. Electrolytes. Urine sent for R/M and C/S. Reports awaited.

PLAN:
- Admit in ward.
- IV Fluids: Start with 1 pint RL stat, then alternate NS and RL.
- INJ EMESET 4mg IV SOS for vomiting.
- INJ PAN-40 40mg IV 1-0-0.
- TAB OFLOX-TZ 1-0-1.
- TAB ENTROL 1-0-1.
- Strict Intake-Output charting. Monitor vitals.
progress_note_day_1:
TIRUMALA MULTISPECIALITY HOSPITAL, HYDERABAD

PROGRESS NOTE
PATIENT NAME: Mr. Prakash Sharma, 52/M
DATE: 11/05/24

S: Patient reports feeling slightly better. Vomiting has stopped. Frequency of loose stools has reduced to 8-10 episodes in last 24 hrs. Passed about 600ml urine since admission. Still feels weak.

O: 
VITALS: BP 100/70 mmHg, PR 96/min, RR 18/min, Temp Afebrile.
General condition: Looks less dehydrated, tongue is moist. Accepting sips of oral fluids.
INVESTIGATIONS:
CBC: Hb 14.5 g/dL, TLC 11,200/cumm (Neutrophilia)
RFT (on admission): Urea 88 mg/dL, Creatinine 1.9 mg/dL
S. Electrolytes: Na+ 130 mEq/L, K+ 3.9 mEq/L

A: Acute Gastroenteritis with pre-renal AKI and Hyponatremia, showing signs of improvement with hydration.

P: 
- Continue IV fluids (NS + 20Kcl) at 100ml/hr.
- Continue INJ PAN-40 1-0-0.
- Continue TAB OFLOX-TZ 1-0-1 and TAB ENTROL 1-0-1.
- INJ EMESET SOS.
- Encourage oral rehydration with ORS and soft diet as tolerated.
- Repeat RFT and electrolytes in the morning.
- Await Urine Culture report.
progress_note_day_2:
TIRUMALA MULTISpeciality HOSPITAL, HYDERABAD

PROGRESS NOTE
PATIENT NAME: Mr. Prakash Sharma, 52/M
DATE: 12/05/24

S: Patient feels much better today. No episodes of vomiting. Passed 2 semi-formed stools since morning. Tolerating soft diet and oral fluids well. No giddiness or weakness.

O: 
VITALS: BP 120/80 mmHg, PR 82/min, RR 16/min, Temp Afebrile.
General condition: Looks well-hydrated, active and comfortable. Abdomen is soft.
INVESTIGATIONS:
Repeat RFT: Urea 45 mg/dL, Creatinine 1.2 mg/dL
Repeat S. Electrolytes: Na+ 136 mEq/L

A: Resolving Gastroenteritis. AKI and electrolyte imbalance corrected. Patient is hemodynamically stable and fit for discharge.

P:
- IV cannula removed. Shift to oral medications completely.
- Stop home medication TAB TELMA-H for 2 more days, then restart.
- Discharge planned for today with advice.
- Continue antibiotics and supportive medications.
- Explain discharge medications and follow-up plan.

discharge_advice:
TIRUMALA MULTISPECIALITY HOSPITAL, HYDERABAD
DISCHARGE SUMMARY

PATIENT NAME: Mr. Prakash Sharma
AGE/SEX: 52/M
UHID: 240510-9832
DATE OF ADMISSION: 10/05/24
DATE OF DISCHARGE: 12/05/24

DIAGNOSIS:
1. Acute Gastroenteritis with moderate dehydration (Resolved)
2. Pre-renal Azotemia (Resolved)
3. Hyponatremia (Corrected)
4. Hypertension

COURSE IN THE HOSPITAL:
Mr. Prakash Sharma was admitted with complaints of loose stools, vomiting and decreased urine output. Investigations revealed dehydration, hyponatremia and acute kidney injury. He was managed conservatively with IV fluids, antibiotics and other supportive care. His symptoms resolved, and his kidney function and electrolytes normalized. He is now hemodynamically stable and tolerating oral diet.

CONDITION AT DISCHARGE:
Stable, afebrile, well-hydrated. Vitals are normal. Accepting oral fluids and diet.

ADVICE ON DISCHARGE:
| No | Medication Name | Dosage | Frequency | Duration |
|----|-----------------|--------|-----------|----------|
| 1  | TAB AZITHRAL    | 500mg  | 1-0-0     | 3 Days   |
| 2  | TAB PAN-40      | 40mg   | 1-0-0 (Pre-BF)| 5 Days   |
| 3  | TAB ENTROL      | 100mg  | 1-0-1     | 3 Days   |
| 4  | TAB DOLO-650    | 650mg  | SOS       | As needed|

- Continue plenty of oral fluids (water, ORS, coconut water).
- Take a soft, bland diet. Avoid oily and spicy food for one week.
- Stop TAB TELMA-H for two more days, then restart your regular dose.

FOLLOW-UP INSTRUCTIONS:
- Review in the General Medicine OPD with Dr. R. Mehta after 5 days.
- Please come back to the emergency room immediately if you develop high fever, severe abdominal pain, recurrence of vomiting or decreased urine output.

PENDING RESULTS:
- Urine Culture & Sensitivity Report. Please collect the report during your follow-up visit.
injected_messiness: A Urine Culture & Sensitivity report is listed as 'Report Awaited' on the lab report and 'Pending' on the discharge summary.
The antibiotic was changed from TAB OFLOX-TZ on admission to TAB AZITHRAL at discharge without a documented reason in the progress notes.

The admission diagnosis lists 'Acute Kidney Injury (AKI) on evaluation', a broad term, while the discharge diagnosis specifies 'Pre-renal Azotemia' without intervening notes showing the specific workup that confidently ruled out other AKI types.
